caveats: Requires an independent thread to send a packet with command <= SSH_MSG_KEX_LAST (e.g. DISCONNECT via idle/auth timeout, application-initiated disconnect, or exception path) exactly while the IO thread executes the cipher swap in receiveNewKeys; timing-dependent but no stall or special scheduling is needed since the threads are independent.

The deployment model is unconfirmed: judged as a library where application, timer, and IO threads may call session methods concurrently, which the code's own locking design (encodeLock, sessionLock, timeout listener) anticipates.
A torn pair corrupts the wire packet only if the two reads straddle the writes; with an unchanged renegotiated cipher the sizes match and the tear is benign.
subclaims.reason: In T3, the IO dispatch thread swaps the outbound crypto parameters with no encode lock: messageReceived (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/session/helpers/AbstractSession.java:377) -> decode (AbstractSession.java:1466) -> handleMessage (AbstractSession.java:428, holds only sessionLock) -> doHandleMessage NEWKEYS case (AbstractSession.java:480) -> handleNewKeys (AbstractSession.java:733) -> receiveNewKeys, which writes outCipher/outMac/outCompression at AbstractSession.java:1743-1757 and outCipherSize/outMacSize at AbstractSession.java:1759-1760. Concurrently, any other thread can be inside encode(): public SessionHelper.disconnect (sshd-core/src/main/java/org/apache/sshd/common/session/helpers/SessionHelper.java:1139) sends SSH_MSG_DISCONNECT (cmd 1, SshConstants.java:46) which is <= SSH_MSG_KEX_LAST (49, SshConstants.java:58), so enqueuePendingPacket lets it through at AbstractSession.java:921 even mid-kex, reaching doWritePacket (AbstractSession.java:990, holds encodeLock) -> encode, which reads outCipher at AbstractSession.java:1245 and outCipherSize at AbstractSession.java:1249 in separate non-atomic reads. The fields are plain non-volatile (AbstractSession.java:157-167); the swap side never takes encodeLock and the encode side never takes sessionLock (its only acquisition in the tree is AbstractSession.java:428), so no common lock or happens-before edge rules out the swap landing between the two reads, yielding a torn pair (new cipher with old size or vice versa). Side A is the IO dispatch thread processing inbound NEWKEYS; side B is the timeout timer thread (SessionTimeoutListener.java:81 run -> checkForTimeouts -> disconnect), any application thread calling session.disconnect()/writePacket, or a channel worker via exceptionCaught (SessionHelper.java:1245).
